definitions.title: Right-Hand Limit
definitions.statement: The right-hand limit of f(x) as x approaches c is L if f(x) becomes arbitrarily close to L as x approaches c from values strictly greater than c (x > c).
conditions: f is defined on an open interval (c, c + d) for some d > 0
definitions.explanation: Restricting the domain to the right of c allows limits to be evaluated at boundary points of domains (e.g. sqrt(x) at x = 0).
definitions.keyTakeaway: Right-hand limit examines behavior strictly from values greater than c.

definitions.title: Left-Hand Limit
definitions.statement: The left-hand limit of f(x) as x approaches c is L if f(x) becomes arbitrarily close to L as x approaches c from values strictly less than c (x < c).
conditions: f is defined on an open interval (c - d, c) for some d > 0
definitions.explanation: Important for functions with jump discontinuities such as piecewise and step functions.
definitions.keyTakeaway: Left-hand limit examines behavior strictly from values less than c.

definitions.title: Two-Sided Limit Existence Criterion
definitions.latex: \lim_{x \to c} f(x) = L \iff \lim_{x \to c^+} f(x) = L \quad \text{and} \quad \lim_{x \to c^-} f(x) = L
definitions.statement: A function f(x) has a two-sided limit L as x approaches c if and only if both the right-hand and left-hand limits exist and are equal to L.
conditions: Both one-sided limits must exist as finite numbers
Both one-sided limits must equal the exact same real value L
definitions.explanation: If the one-sided limits differ, the two-sided limit does not exist (DNE), typically indicating a jump discontinuity.
definitions.keyTakeaway: Two-sided limit exists if and only if left and right limits agree.

definitions.title: Fundamental Trigonometric Limits
definitions.statement: When angle theta is measured in radians, the ratio of sin(theta) to theta approaches 1 as theta approaches 0.
conditions: theta must be measured in radians
theta approaches 0 from both positive and negative sides
definitions.explanation: Proven geometrically using unit circle sector areas and the Sandwich Theorem: cos(theta) < sin(theta)/theta < 1.
definitions.keyTakeaway: sin(theta) is approximately equal to theta for small radian angles theta.
